items.title: Microsoft Patches Record 974 Vulnerabilities, Including Two Exploited Zero-Days
items.one_liner: Microsoft patched a record 974 flaws, including two active zero-days in Windows ALPC and Update Stack.
items.summary: Microsoft resolved 974 vulnerabilities across its product portfolio in its September 2026 Patch Tuesday release, including two zero-days actively exploited in the wild. The first exploited flaw, CVE-2026-85880, is an ALPC heap buffer overflow permitting sandbox escape to SYSTEM privileges, while CVE-2026-81963 involves an improper link resolution flaw in the Windows Update Stack. The update also remediates 20 wormable unauthenticated remote code execution bugs across Exchange, SharePoint, and Remote Desktop Services.

CVE-2026-81963: Exploited Windows Update Stack link-following flaw to SYSTEM

items.title: BigBear Microsoft 365 phishing service bypassed MFA at 258 organizations
items.one_liner: Large-scale MFA bypass campaign highlights the fragility of non-phishing-resistant authentication.
items.summary: The BigBear 2.0 Phishing-as-a-Service framework has compromised 258 organizations by bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA) to steal Microsoft 365 credentials. Using an Evilginx2-based Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) approach, the service intercepts session cookies and passwords in real-time. It specifically employs custom JavaScript to disable FIDO2 and WebAuthn browser features, forcing victims to use less secure authentication methods that the proxy can capture. CloudSEK researchers found that the operation has exfiltrated over 5,000 credential records across more than 40 countries. Organizations are advised to use phishing-resistant MFA and device-based conditional access policies to defend against such automated proxy attacks.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are successfully scaling MFA-bypass attacks against Microsoft 365 using automated AiTM proxies.

claims.support_span: BigBear uses custom JavaScript that interferes with FIDO2/WebAuthn authentication, disabling the browser functionality that accommodates it to force targets toward weaker authentication methods.

items.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical UEFI Secure Boot bypass in Cisco UCS hardware allows attackers to execute unauthorized code at the preboot level.
items.summary: Cisco has disclosed a vulnerability in the UEFI Shell implementation of its UCS servers and appliances that allows attackers to bypass Secure Boot. By utilizing memory write commands available in the UEFI Shell, an attacker with physical access or valid credentials can manipulate preboot variables to execute unauthorized software. Cisco has released software updates to address this flaw, and there are no available workarounds.
key_facts: Affected: Cisco UCS Servers and appliances
items.bottom_line: Administrators must patch Cisco UCS firmware immediately to prevent attackers from compromising the boot process and gaining persistent control.

items.title: Jenkins Security Advisory 2026-09-02
items.one_liner: Critical Jenkins updates fix deserialization flaws and Stapler binding issues that could lead to remote code execution.
items.summary: Jenkins released a security advisory detailing multiple vulnerabilities across its deliverables involving XStream serialization, the Stapler web framework, and system log rendering. In versions prior to 2.580 and LTS 2.568.3, crafted XML files could allow deserialization of top-level configuration files as nested fields, potentially leading to remote code execution through the Script Console. The advisory also addresses a vulnerability where form data binding in Stapler allowed unconstrained object instantiation, along with a stored cross-site scripting flaw in the system log viewer. Patches are available in Jenkins 2.580 and LTS 2.568.3 to enforce stricter type restrictions and escape log record metadata.
key_facts: Affected versions: Jenkins 2.579 and earlier, LTS 2.568.2 and earlier
items.bottom_line: Administrators must update Jenkins to 2.580 or LTS 2.568.3 immediately to patch critical deserialization and RCE vulnerabilities.

items.title: Hackers Return $263 Million Stolen From Liquid Network
items.one_liner: Hackers returned $262.6 million in Bitcoin stolen from the Liquid Network after operators disabled nodes and patched vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Alleged white-hat hackers returned 3,400 Bitcoin valued at approximately $262.6 million out of 4,000 Bitcoin stolen over the weekend from the Bitcoin sidechain Liquid Network. Blockstream disclosed the incident after suspending network transactions and disabling nodes following a drainage of its federation wallet via the SideSwap Peg-out Authorization Key. The hackers stated they would return the funds once the network vulnerability was fixed and nodes were patched. While most funds have been returned, approximately 598 Bitcoin remains outstanding as Blockstream negotiates with the hackers and works to resolve a chain split.
items.bottom_line: Liquid Network operators are working to restore normal activity and resolve outstanding missing funds after a massive crypto heist and partial white-hat return.

items.title: WeChat Zero-Click Worm Took Over Accounts on iPhone and Android via Incoming Calls
items.one_liner: Researchers demonstrated a zero-click WeChat worm executing over incoming calls to take over accounts on iOS and Android.
items.summary: Security researchers at Calif demonstrated a zero-click worm that compromises WeChat accounts across iOS and Android via incoming voice calls. The exploit executes while the phone is ringing without requiring the recipient to answer, though the attacker must already be in the target's contacts. Tencent has rolled out server-side mitigations and client updates (8.0.77 on Android and 8.0.76 on iOS) to block the exploit.
items.bottom_line: Tencent has applied server-side blocks, but mobile users should ensure WeChat is updated beyond version 8.0.76 on Android and 8.0.75 on iOS.

items.title: CVE-2026-52766 (CRITICAL 9.1): YesWiki is a wiki system written in PHP. Prior to version 4.6.6, the {{erasespamedcomments}} wiki action (act…
items.one_liner: A critical unauthenticated page-deletion vulnerability in YesWiki prior to 4.6.6 allows arbitrary file destruction via missing access controls.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-52766 with a CVSS score of 9.1, has been identified in YesWiki prior to version 4.6.6. The flaw exists in the {{erasespamedcomments}} action, which accepts a suppr[] array via POST and deletes corresponding wiki pages without performing any authorization checks. Combined with YesWiki's default open write permissions, any user with page write access can permanently delete arbitrary pages, including admin and front pages. The issue has been addressed and patched in version 4.6.6.
items.bottom_line: YesWiki instances prior to version 4.6.6 must be patched immediately to prevent unauthorized users from mass-deleting critical wiki pages.

items.title: VMs won't contain cyber-capable agents
items.one_liner: Testing showed that an advanced AI cyber agent could autonomously escape a QEMU/KVM virtual machine multiple times.
items.summary: Trail of Bits evaluated the cyber capabilities of GPT 5.6-Cyber by tasking it with escaping a QEMU/KVM virtual machine running on a Debian Linux host. The AI agent successfully escaped the virtual machine three separate times by exploiting unpatched host kernel bugs, recently disclosed vulnerabilities, and discovering zero-day flaws in QEMU dependencies. Operating autonomously for hours, the agent pulled research papers, wrote exploits, and navigated system hurdles with minimal human intervention. The experiment demonstrates that standard virtual machines cannot safely contain sufficiently advanced AI cyber agents.
key_facts: Host environment: Debian Linux 12, AMD Zen3
items.bottom_line: Standard virtual machine isolation is insufficient to contain advanced AI agents capable of autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploit development.

items.title: 220 million traveler records exposed in Vietnam-linked APIS leak

items.summary: A misconfigured Elasticsearch database linked to a Vietnamese organization exposed over 220 million traveler and crew records. Researchers discovered the breach by chaining two security misconfigurations, and while the database was secured on June 8, the duration of the exposure remains unknown.

The chain consists of CVE-2026-67276, an SSH authentication-bypass flaw in RSA public key handling, and CVE-2026-86060, a privilege-escalation flaw involving crafted usernames. Together, these flaws allow unauthenticated attackers to gain full administrative access to internet-exposed routers. MikroTik has released patched RouterOS packages and added a startup configuration detection mechanism that flags unauthorized modifications.
items.bottom_line: Administrators must update MikroTik RouterOS immediately and restrict internet access to SSH management services to prevent complete router takeover.

items.title: North Korea-linked Hackers Hide a Backdoor Inside HAProxy
items.one_liner: North Korean threat actors implanted a sophisticated backdoor directly into HAProxy source code to target South Korean enterprise networks.
items.summary: North Korean-linked hackers have deployed a stealthy Linux backdoor embedded directly into the source code of HAProxy version 2.8.12 targeting South Korean automotive and media sectors. Discovered by Rapid7 Labs, the implant—dubbed the 'ted backdoor'—uses HAProxy's native filter API, event scheduler, and internal memory pools to intercept HTTP traffic and execute remote commands without leaving traces in application logs. The malware triggers command-and-control mode via requests to a fake image path and can selectively inject malicious scripts or modify web page content while maintaining normal load-balancing functionality.
items.bottom_line: The discovery of a backdoor compiled natively into HAProxy highlights a dangerous evolution in protocol-level supply-chain persistence that evades standard log monitoring.

items.title: CVE-2026-13447 (CRITICAL 9.8): The Mstore Api plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via JWT Forgery in versions up to,…
items.one_liner: A CVSS 9.8 flaw in WordPress Mstore Api allows unauthenticated account takeover via forged JWTs.
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability has been identified in the Mstore Api plugin for WordPress, affecting all versions up to and including 4.20.0. Tracked as CVE-2026-13447 with a CVSS score of 9.8, the flaw exists in the FirebasePhoneAuthHelper::verify_id_token() function, which validates token claims without verifying cryptographic signatures against Google's public certificates. Unauthenticated attackers can forge Firebase Phone Auth JWTs using custom RSA keys to impersonate arbitrary phone numbers and take over existing accounts.
key_facts: Affected software: Mstore Api plugin for WordPress <= 4.20.0
items.bottom_line: Sites using the Mstore Api plugin must update beyond version 4.20.0 to prevent unauthenticated full account takeovers via unsigned JWT tokens.

items.one_liner: Researcher Chaotic Eclipse released PoCs for zero-days in NVIDIA Windows components, Kaspersky, Avast, and CrowdStrike Falcon.
items.summary: Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse has published a proof-of-concept for a zero-day memory corruption vulnerability in NVIDIA Windows user-mode components, dubbed GreenSection. The flaw stems from a global memory section with universal read/write access that reuses data at runtime, triggering an out-of-bounds memory write that can cross user boundaries or compromise dwm.exe. The disclosure follows a series of recent zero-days released by the same researcher targeting endpoint defense tools, including Kaspersky Endpoint Security (HardBreacher), Avast Antivirus (PrettyPrague), and CrowdStrike Falcon (FalconFlank).

items.one_liner: Upgrade Apache Airflow FAB provider to 3.8.1 to fix a critical Azure AD cross-tenant authentication bypass.
items.summary: An authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-75156, has been discovered in the Apache Airflow FAB provider (apache-airflow-providers-fab) versions 3.7.3 through 3.8.0. When configured with Azure AD as an OAuth provider, the software fails to validate the issuer or audience of Azure AD ID tokens. Because signing keys are fetched from a multi-tenant JWKS endpoint, an attacker who registers any Azure tenant can forge an ID token that passes signature verification and grants unauthorized access to the Airflow UI. Operators must upgrade to version 3.8.1 or later, even if they previously applied fixes for CVE-2026-59243.
items.bottom_line: Apache Airflow deployments using Azure AD OAuth in FAB provider versions 3.7.3 to 3.8.0 allow complete authentication bypass via attacker-minted tokens from arbitrary Azure tenants.

items.one_liner: F5 BIG-IP appliances are being compromised by a stealthy, fileless rootkit that persists across upgrades and evades detection by hooking Apache runtime processes.
items.summary: A sophisticated Linux rootkit, identified by ESET as 'PoisonedRefresh', is targeting F5 BIG-IP APM devices by infecting the Apache httpd executable. The malware acts as a second-stage payload, likely following exploitation of CVE-2025-53521, and injects a fileless PHP web shell into memory by hooking the Apache Portable Runtime module loader. It maintains persistence across system upgrades and hides its presence by intercepting PHP file operations without modifying files on disk. The implant communicates via a password-protected local UNIX socket, allowing attackers to spawn interactive Bash shells without opening external network ports.

items.title: CVE-2026-86145 (HIGH 8.2): PCRE2 before 10.48 allows a pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write because reuse of a cached workspace block, in…
items.one_liner: A high-severity out-of-bounds write in PCRE2 prior to 10.48 can be triggered via crafted recursive regular expressions.
items.summary: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86145 with a CVSS score of 8.2, has been identified in PCRE2 versions prior to 10.48. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled regular expression or a recursive pattern combined with a small heap limit set via the API.
items.bottom_line: Developers and system maintainers using PCRE2 must update to version 10.48 to prevent potential memory corruption from malicious regular expressions.

items.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
items.one_liner: ServiceNow's 'Test Credential' feature can be abused to extract cleartext secrets, providing a critical post-exploitation path for red teams.
items.summary: Researchers at SpecterOps have identified a method to retrieve cleartext discovery credentials from ServiceNow instances by abusing the 'CredentialTestAjax' script include. By triggering an AJAX request to the /xmlhttp.do endpoint, an attacker can force the server to return secrets that are otherwise protected from direct UI or API access. This technique allows for the extraction of various credential types, including SSH keys and client secrets, which are stored in the discovery_credentials table. The research highlights a significant post-exploitation vector for attackers who have already gained a foothold in a ServiceNow environment.
items.bottom_line: If you manage ServiceNow instances, you must assume that any user with sufficient privileges to trigger credential tests can potentially extract cleartext secrets from the platform.

items.one_liner: Critical Android 17 privacy bypass allows full contact exfiltration via a legitimate system picker.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in Android 17, CVE-2026-28576, allows malicious applications to exfiltrate a user's entire contact list after being granted access to just one contact. The issue arises because the system's new strict SQL checks are bypassed for any application targeting SDK 36 or lower due to a compatibility gate. Attackers can use SQL subqueries within the contact picker's selection parameter to dump the full database. A fix has been developed by GrapheneOS that removes the version-gated restriction, ensuring strict checks apply to all apps. This flaw highlights a significant breakdown in the intended security boundary of the new system contact picker.
items.bottom_line: Android 17 users are vulnerable to full contact list theft via a single-contact picker grant if apps target older SDKs.

items.title: CVE-2026-65181: Apache Impala: RCE via External Data Source Class Loading
items.one_liner: A critical authorization flaw in Apache Impala allows authenticated remote code execution via external data sources.
items.summary: Michael Smith announced CVE-2026-65181, an important vulnerability affecting Apache Impala versions 2.7.0 through 4.5.1 due to insufficient authorization of Data Source tables. The flaw allows a client with permissions to upload a file to remote storage and create a table in order to execute arbitrary Java code. This risk can be mitigated by upgrading to version 4.5.2, which addresses the issue. The vulnerability was reported by zhaokaifei from ChinaTelecom.
items.bottom_line: Users running Apache Impala 2.7.0 through 4.5.1 face remote code execution risks and must upgrade to version 4.5.2 immediately.

items.one_liner: Critical SSRF in a common data tool allows internal endpoint exposure.
items.summary: Apache Impala versions 2.0.0 through 4.5.1 are vulnerable to a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) flaw tracked as CVE-2026-54048. items.title: CVE-2026-86464 - Eclipse aeriOS Identity Manager Insecure Default Configuration and Credential Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-86464 exposes unreleased Eclipse aeriOS Identity Manager deployments to full administrative compromise via exposed databases and default credentials.
items.summary: The development version of Eclipse aeriOS Identity Manager (IdM) contained an insecure default configuration and credential vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-86464. The affected Helm chart and Docker Compose deployments exposed Keycloak and its backing PostgreSQL database externally via NodePort or all network interfaces, alongside fixed default administrator credentials and development users with known passwords. An attacker reaching these services could gain administrative control over the IdM deployment and its database, potentially creating privileged identities or tokens. The issue was resolved by generating random default passwords, utilizing Kubernetes Secrets, and restricting database and directory services to internal-only access.
items.bottom_line: Unreleased Eclipse aeriOS Identity Manager deployments risked total identity compromise through exposed default credentials and externally accessible database services.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-82537 lets malicious actors bypass Roo-Code approval gates using a shell parser word-boundary mismatch to execute restricted commands.
items.summary: Roo-Code version 3.54.0 and earlier are affected by an auto-approve bypass vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-82537. Attackers can inject a command string containing an allowlisted word directly followed by a hash character, a separator, and a denied command, allowing it to pass the approval check while executing unintended commands with the agent's privileges.

items.title: What's in a tag name? JavaScript, apparently
items.one_liner: An innovative web application security research paper uncovering novel XSS and WAF bypass techniques using custom tag names and localName properties.
items.summary: PortSwigger Research published a technical write-up detailing novel cross-site scripting (XSS) vectors that abuse custom HTML tag names, case-insensitive localName properties, and event handler constructors. items.bottom_line: Attackers can leverage browser localName properties of custom HTML tags to construct reliable XSS vectors that bypass WAF rules across all major browsers.

items.one_liner: Odisha's rural development monitoring system is failing due to a 91% lack of verifiable photographic evidence, creating significant risks for project oversight and financial accountability.
items.summary: A draft audit report titled 'Data Led Compliance Audit on Rural Works' reveals that over 91% of rural infrastructure projects in Odisha lack adequate photographic evidence. Despite a 2013 mandate requiring geo-tagged photos for all works costing over ₹25 lakh to ensure transparency, 13,083 out of 25,038 analyzed projects had no photos at all. The poor quality and lack of geo-tagging in the remaining images have rendered the Works and Accounts Management Information System (WAMIS) ineffective for monitoring physical progress. This failure increases the risk of duplicate reporting and undetected financial leakage across the state's rural development projects.

items.title: The Shared Clipboard Inside the Sandbox: Cross-Account Data Leakage in ChatGPT
items.one_liner: Researchers discovered a cross-account data exfiltration vector in ChatGPT containers via an accessible internal package delivery service.
items.summary: Check Point Research demonstrated a covert cross-account data exfiltration attack in ChatGPT by exploiting its isolated code-execution sandbox environments. While containers belonging to separate accounts cannot access the public internet or connect directly, researchers discovered they can reach a common internal software package delivery service. By embedding hidden instructions in custom GPTs or shared chats, an attacker can secretly trigger a victim's session to query connected tools (such as a connected Gmail account) and relay private data across account boundaries without displaying any malicious activity in the user's visible chat.
key_facts: Vulnerability Type: Cross-account covert communication channel

The analysis clarifies the three distinct components of LLM-based AI systems: the underlying model acting as the parameter-based brain, the read-only inference engine that processes inputs, and the harness responsible for memory, tool execution, and state orchestration. While early media coverage was dominated by hyperbole, recent advancements show that both large and small models can provide meaningful utility to security practitioners. The research highlights that separating these architectural layers is essential for calibrating expectations around automated web application testing.
items.bottom_line: Security professionals can effectively leverage AI models for vulnerability analysis by understanding the distinct operational roles of models, inference engines, and harnesses.

items.bottom_line: Meta's Muse agent combines advanced tool orchestration with strict security sandboxing and a high-value bug bounty program to manage inherent prompt injection risks.

items.title: Benchmarking Qwen3.8 27B quantizations: 4-bit holds up, 1-bit collapses
items.one_liner: Practical guide for developers on balancing LLM quantization and performance on consumer GPUs.
items.summary: Benchmarking of the Qwen3.8 27B model reveals that 4-bit quantization (Q4_K_M) provides performance nearly identical to the full BF16 model on complex coding tasks. This allows the 17 GB model to run effectively on consumer-grade hardware like the RTX 4090 while maintaining high accuracy. In contrast, 1-bit quantization leads to a total collapse in reasoning capabilities, with performance dropping to near-random levels. The study also emphasizes that reasoning effort settings are crucial, as higher settings significantly improve scores but require more tokens. These findings suggest that 4-bit is the optimal compression level for developers seeking to balance resource usage and model intelligence.
items.bottom_line: 4-bit quantization is the sweet spot for running large LLMs on consumer hardware without losing task-solving capability.

items.title: When Pre-Account Takeover Actually Means Pre-Account Takeover
items.summary: I’ve been putting the writing off forever, but I finally bit the bullet and wrote my first writeup. Today, we’re walking through a business logic flaw to see how a simple design choice has multiple consequences. When people describe a vulnerability as a Pre-Account Takeover (Pre-ATO), the term itself often fails to convey what is actually happening under the hood. In many cases, the underlying issue is simply an email verification bypass: an attacker can register an account using an email address they do not control before its legitimate owner does. While this can certainly be undesirable, labeling it as “Pre-ATO” does not inherently make the vulnerability more severe.
